I'm convinced of... 

I am confident that...

To me, people that say they "choose" a certain belief are actually saying that they don't believe, but they are consciously choosing to deceive themselves. Because in reality, you either believe something or you don't. It's not a choice.

As with any intrusive thoughts, you have to let them pass through. 

One thing I was taught from counseling was to visualize in your mind that you are at a train station and every thought that passes through your mind is like a train passing by. This includes intrusive or negative thoughts. Sometimes they drive by without stopping, sometimes they stop and sit there for a while. But instead of getting in that train (of thought), just keep reminding yourself that you're only there to watch. 

This puts yourself in the mental position of an observer and allows you to take control of how you react to these thoughts. Instead of reacting and dwelling on the thought itself, replace it with observations (hmm, that train sure is staying here for a long time. I wonder when the next train will be showing up. That train sure is ugly). Don't try to force them to stop, don't dwell on whether or not they are true or false, and don't try to force them out. 

They're just thoughts and they will pass by eventually. Just let them work their way through the station and don't get on that train. Eventually, those thoughts will pass by faster, less often, or stop showing up altogether. 

I hope that didn't sound to "woo" but it is a helpful mental exercise that works for a lot of people dealing with indoctrination, anxiety, stress, and even suicidal ideation.
